dedupe_keys.name: iso new england energy water nexus enterprise control assessment of six 2040 scenarios

description: This paper assesses how water supply and treatment systems and water-dependent power plants could be operated flexibly to help balance the ISO New England electricity grid as nuclear, coal and oil retire and wind and solar grow. Muhanji, Barrows, Macknick and Farid used the Electric Power Enterprise Control System simulator for grid operation and the System-Level Generic Model for water use, and compared six scenarios for 2040 on power imbalances, operating reserves, market production costs and water withdrawals and consumption. Coverage is the six New England states' grid. In scenarios with high shares of variable renewables, water resources could give load-following, ramping and regulation reserves and reduce cost and water use. Format and access: an open arXiv preprint under CC BY 4.0, with no data release read. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: a model study of future scenarios, not observed operations, using simulators the paper introduces from earlier work. It supports capacity planning and resilience studies of coupled water and power operation. A related catalogue record is the interdependent water and power infrastructure model.
